AI and learning

Generated view: 15 sources whose Kunskapsbank note was filed under this theme, and the claims and candidates they link to.

Claims

C2 alive

When learners use an AI tool that hands them finished answers or solutions while they practise, their scores on the practice work go up, but what they have learned is lower when it is later measured without the tool.

Serves: Q2 (How do we achieve optimal learning when AI and screens are everywhere?)
Ages: grundskola-hog, gymnasium, vuxen-livslangt (evidence: upper-secondary maths in Turkey, grades 7–12 in one Chinese county, a university lab); not yet shown for younger pupils or in Swedish classrooms

Bounds: Evidence in the bank: Bastani et al. 2024 (upper-secondary maths RCT, Turkey: answer-giving GPT Base +48 % correct answers during practice, −17 % on the closed-book exam compared with pupils who never had GenAI); Strömberg, Lei & Wu 2026 (secondary-school DiD in one Chinese county, conference paper, results may be revised: homework scores +18 %, monthly closed-book tests −20 % within six months, entrance exams −18 to −24 % with the full penalty visible after about two years); Fan et al. 2025 (university lab, second-language essay: ChatGPT raised essay scores but not knowledge gain or transfer). The loss is concentrated in "homework outsourcing" use (about 80 % of AI users in Strömberg et al.); users who keep study time similar to non-users show small losses. The claim is about learning measured without the tool; performance with the tool goes up. Positive pooled effects in ChatGPT/chatbot meta-analyses (Deng et al. 2025, Doo & Park 2026, Wu & Yu 2024, Fan et al. 2026) are recorded as challenges, because the bank notes that most of their outcomes were not measured without the tool.

Attack record: No attacks yet · Evidence links: 9 linked sources (4 supports, 3 limits, 4 challenges)

Candidates (not approved)

  • K15: Unprotected answer-giving GPT harms upper-secondary closed-book learning, while a tutor version that withholds answers is pedagogically different and mitigates the harm. (1 link(s))
  • K16: ChatGPT use improves student learning (Deng et al. 2025 meta-analysis). (1 link(s))
  • K17: ChatGPT raises learning achievement (Doo & Park 2026 meta-analysis). (1 link(s))
  • K19: GenAI improves learning outcomes (Fan et al. 2026 meta-analysis, higher education). (1 link(s))
  • K21: Undesigned, free GenAI use does not systematically raise closed-book learning in K–12 without AI-literacy requirements (position of Kasneci et al. 2023). (1 link(s))
  • K22: Intelligent tutoring systems raise K–12 learning compared with business as usual, but effects on standardised tests are much smaller than on local tests. (1 link(s))
  • K23: Intelligent tutoring systems outperform non-ITS computer-based instruction on standardised K–12 measures when content coverage is equal. (1 link(s))
  • K25: A guard-railed AI tutor inside a mastery requirement gives better delayed closed-book learning than the same platform without AI. (1 link(s))
  • K26: A coaching AI (Khanmigo) adds to standardised maths only when pupils actually engage in substantive dialogue with it. (1 link(s))
  • K28: Well-designed step-based tutoring systems come close to human tutoring, and answer-giving GenAI without guardrails does not match them on closed-book outcomes. (1 link(s))
  • K30: AI chatbots improve students' learning outcomes (Wu & Yu 2024 meta-analysis). (1 link(s))

Former theme summary (Swedish, from the Kunskapsbank archive)

Tema: AI och lärande

Djupdykning 1 (AI-001–004) + C (AI-005–010) + gap ITS/GenAI-K12 (AI-011–015) 2026-09-07. Fokus: GenAI, designad ITS, K–12 closed-book, cognitive offloading.

Synteser i denna mapp

Tvärgående slutsats (uppdaterad)

  1. Meta g ≈ 0,5–0,7 under experimentella villkor (Fan 2026; Doo & Park; Deng) — men prestation ≠ lärande.
  2. Closed-book efter GenAI: skada i RCT (Bastani −17 %) och storskalig K–12 DiD (Strömberg läxa +18 % / prov −20 %).
  3. Mekanism: crutch / homework outsourcing / metacognitive laziness (Bastani; Strömberg; Fan 2025).
  4. Tutoring med guardrails mildrar skada (Bastani) och kan ge modest delayed vinst vs CAL när mastery+no-answer (NUMI AI-014); Khanmigo (AI-015) begränsas av engagemang. Pre-GenAI ITS (AI-011–013) är steelman för designad digital tutor.
  5. Svensk praktik (Skolverket AI-010): lärare anpassar redan bedömning; efterfrågar fortbildning — policy bör styra mot skyddad productive struggle (Kasneci).
